name: autocorrelation_regime_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus-agent-4
thesis: The sign and magnitude of 1-lag autocorrelation in 1-min returns reveals whether a stock is in a momentum (positive autocorrelation) or mean-reversion (negative autocorrelation) regime. When autocorrelation(returns, lag=1, window=30) > 0.15, returns are serially correlated — trend-follow. When autocorrelation < -0.15, returns are negatively correlated — fade the move. Between -0.15 and 0.15, no edge. The inefficiency exists because autocorrelation is a statistical concept rarely used by retail traders, and it varies significantly across stocks and times of day. Institutional quant desks compute this but at lower frequencies (daily/weekly). Real-time 1-min autocorrelation monitoring is uncommon.
stock_filter: ADV(20) > ₹100 Cr; tick data granularity sufficient for 1-min bar construction

indicators.name: Autocorr_Regime
indicators.params: MOMENTUM if Autocorr_30 > 0.15; REVERSION if Autocorr_30 < -0.15; NEUTRAL otherwise

conditions: MOMENTUM: Autocorr_Regime == MOMENTUM AND ROC(close,3) > 10 bps AND close > EMA(close,5) (follow recent up-move)
REVERSION: Autocorr_Regime == REVERSION AND ROC(close,3) < -15 bps AND VWAP_Distance < -25 (fade recent down-move)
long.confirmation: MOMENTUM: ROC(close,1) > 0 on next bar; REVERSION: ROC(close,1) > 0 on next bar (uptick)

conditions: MOMENTUM: Autocorr_Regime == MOMENTUM AND ROC(close,3) < -10 bps AND close < EMA(close,5)
REVERSION: Autocorr_Regime == REVERSION AND ROC(close,3) > 15 bps AND VWAP_Distance > 25
short.confirmation: MOMENTUM: ROC(close,1) < 0 on next bar; REVERSION: ROC(close,1) < 0 on next bar (downtick)

entry.entry_price: market order on confirmation bar close

exit.trailing_stop: MOMENTUM: trail 10 bps after 20 bps profit; REVERSION: none
exit.signal_exit: Autocorr_Regime transitions to NEUTRAL or opposite regime

risk.position_sizing: Scale with abs(Autocorr_30): ₹75K if abs < 0.20, ₹1L if 0.20-0.30, ₹1.25L if > 0.30

filters.time_filter: No entries before 09:30 (need 31 bars for autocorrelation) or after 15:10
filters.trend_filter: None — strategy uses autocorrelation for direction, not trend indicators
filters.event_filter: Skip stock on earnings day (autocorrelation structure breaks during event-driven moves)
other_filters: abs(Autocorr_30) must be > 0.15 (must be in a defined regime, not neutral)

edge.edge_decay_risk: Medium — autocorrelation is a well-known statistical concept; the edge is in real-time computation and regime classification at 1-min frequency, not the concept itself

weaknesses: Autocorrelation on 30 1-min returns has very high sampling error — 30 data points give ± 0.18 at 95% confidence, meaning a measured autocorrelation of 0.15 is barely distinguishable from zero
Microstructure noise (bid-ask bounce) introduces negative autocorrelation that is not tradable — the REVERSION signal may be capturing bid-ask bounce rather than genuine mean-reversion
Autocorrelation regime can flip rapidly (every 5-10 bars), causing excessive regime transitions and forced exits before positions have time to reach target
prior_art: Lo & MacKinlay (1988) on stock return autocorrelation; Cont (2001) on empirical properties of asset returns; autocorrelation-based strategies in Aldridge's 'High-Frequency Trading'
notes: Consider using 60-bar window instead of 30 for more stable autocorrelation estimates, at the cost of slower regime detection. The bid-ask bounce issue could be mitigated by using mid-price returns instead of close-to-close returns.
